title: Fix invalid selectors
author: snowystinger
summary: Makes `:has()` unforgiving and disallows pseudo-elements inside it, so `:has(::before)`, `:has()` and `:not(:has(::backdrop))` become parse errors (warnings + dropped rule in errorRecovery), matching browsers. Today Lightning CSS silently rewrites them into different invalid or even valid selectors; it bit react-spectrum.
evidence: master 574eee2 CLI: `video:not(:has(::backdrop)){color:red}` -> `video:not(:has()){color:red}`; `a:has(::before){color:red}` -> `a:has(:before){color:red}`; `foo:has()` passes through. Chromium 153: CSS.supports('selector(:has(::before))')=false, ':has()'=false, ':has(:before)'=false, 'a:has(b, ::before)'=false. Separate master bug in #1239 not covered by this PR: `a:is(::before)` -> `a:is()`, `b:where(::before, .x)` -> `b:where(.x)`. Small, focused change in selectors/parser.rs; no competing PR; no reviews. Per calibration, check upstream stylo selectors for the matching :has change.
